sentences.text: This painting may hide the loneliest feeling ever given to a creature built like a god.
This is The Demon Seated, painted by Mikhail Vrubel in 1890.
And this isn't a devil with horns.
It's a young giant among stone flowers.
Strong, silent, almost gentle.
But look at his eyes.
He's waiting.
There's a shadow under the eye turned away from you.
And yet it doesn't feel like evil at all.
Look into his eyes.
There's sorrow there.
A heavy, quiet, endless sorrow.
As if he already knows nobody will come for him.
According to Lermontov's poem, this demon fell in love, had his hopes dashed, and was finally crushed.
And Vrubel seems to paint something rarely shown.
Not the demon's fall, but the long silence after it.
The moment when he understands there is no place left for him.
Imagine wanting love and being shut out of your world for it.
Would you keep hoping?
Would you ask for forgiveness?
Or would you start planning your revenge?
That's what makes this painting so unsettling.
The demon is still beautiful, but his eyes no longer look hopeful.
His calm mouth says one thing, his tired eyes say another.
And maybe that is the worst of it.
Maybe evil does not begin with hatred.
Maybe it begins with longing, then becomes loneliness, and eventually turns into sorrow.
So look at him one more time.
Do you see a monster waiting for his revenge?
Or a lonely spirit nobody ever answered?

meta.title: The demon who was never evil, only alone
meta.description: The Demon Seated was painted by Mikhail Vrubel in 1890 after Lermontov's poem The Demon. Vrubel called his demon a spirit not so much evil as suffering and sorrowing.
meta.question: A monster waiting for revenge, or a lonely spirit?

sources.claim: The Demon Seated  (Russian: Демон сидящий) is an 1890 symbolist piece by Russian artist Mikhail Vrubel.
The painting is created in Vrubel's unique style with the effect of crystal edges, which makes his paintings look like stained glasses or panels.

Vrubel described this Demon as “a spirit uniting in itself masculine and feminine qualities…a spirit, not so much evil as suffering and sorrowing, but in all that a powerful spirit…a majestic spirit”.
